t.1.168.2: This is King Kalmāṣapāda, mighty and renowned on earth; it is he who dwells in this region of the forest, exceedingly terrifying.
t.1.168.1: Do not be afraid, daughter; you need have no fear of the rākṣasa at all. This one whom you see standing near is not a rākṣasa from whom any danger comes.
t.1.168.3: Seeing him rushing toward him, the blessed seer Vasiṣṭha, full of splendor, held him back with a mere cry of "huṃ," O Bhārata.
t.1.168.4: And then, sprinkling him with water purified by mantras, he freed that best of kings from the terrible Rākṣasa.
t.1.168.5: For twelve years he had been seized by the very power of Vasiṣṭha, as the sun is seized by the eclipsing planet at the time of the parvan.
t.1.168.6: Then the king, released by the Rākṣasa, lit up that great forest with his radiance, as the sun colors a twilight cloud.
t.1.168.7: Then, having regained consciousness, the king saluted him with joined palms and, at the proper time, spoke to Vasiṣṭha, the best of seers.
t.1.168.8: I am Saudāsa, O greatly fortunate one, your patron for sacrifice, O best of the twice-born. Tell me what you desire at this time; what shall I do for you?
t.1.168.9: This has come to pass in accordance with time. Go, and rule that kingdom of yours; and never, O lord of men, show contempt for brāhmaṇas.
t.1.168.10: The king said: O brahmin, I shall never again disrespect the bulls among brahmins; abiding always by your command, I shall honor the twice-born.
t.1.168.11: But, O best of the twice-born, I wish to obtain from you that boon by which I may become free of my debt to the Ikṣvākus, O best of those who know the Vedas.
t.1.168.13: Then Vasiṣṭha, the best of the twice-born, true to his word, replied there to that king, the supreme archer, saying, "I shall give it."
t.1.168.12: For the sake of offspring, you should go to my beloved queen, who is endowed with virtue, beauty and fine qualities, for the increase of the Ikṣvāku lineage.
t.1.168.14: Then in due time, O sinless one, the lord of men, accompanied by Vasiṣṭha, returned to Ayodhyā, the finest of cities, renowned throughout the worlds.
t.1.168.15: Then all the subjects, rejoicing, went out to meet him, the great-souled one now freed from sin, as the dwellers of heaven go forth to meet their lord.
t.1.168.16: Soon that lord of men entered the city of those of meritorious deeds, accompanied by the great-souled Vasiṣṭha.
t.1.168.17: Then, O king, the people dwelling in Ayodhyā beheld him, united with Puṣya, like the sun risen at its proper time.
t.1.168.18: For he, the foremost of the glorious, filled that Ayodhyā with splendor, as the cool-rayed moon, risen in the autumn season, fills the sky.
t.1.168.20: Then, O joy of the Kurus, that city, crowded with contented and well-nourished people, shone because of him, as Amarāvatī shines with Śakra.
t.1.168.19: That excellent city, its roads sprinkled and swept clean and adorned with raised banners, gladdened his mind.
t.1.168.21: Then, when that king, the lord of kings, had entered the city, the queen, at the command of that king, approached Vasiṣṭha.
t.1.168.23: Then, when the embryo had been conceived in her, that best of sages, saluted respectfully by the king, went back again to his hermitage.
t.1.168.22: Then, at the queen's season, that great seer Vasiṣṭha, the seer endowed with the highest excellence, united with her according to a divine rite.
t.1.168.24: When she did not give birth to the embryo she had carried for a long time, the queen then split open her own womb with a stone.
t.1.168.25: Then, in the twelfth year, O bull among men, he was born: the royal sage named Aśmaka, who founded Potana.
